name: Uhl Anomaly

criteria.description: Congenital partial or complete absence of right ventricular myocardium
Marked dilation of the right ventricle with thin, parchment-like wall
Presence of ventricular arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities
Clinical signs of right ventricular failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence of right ventricular myocardium with right ventricular dilation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and histopathological findings; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right ventricular dilation with thin wall

rare.symptomName: Right bundle branch block on ECG

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to right heart failure
Normal cardiac biomarkers unless secondary injury
imaging: Echocardiography showing absent or severely thinned right ventricular myocardium
Cardiac MRI demonstrating right ventricular myocardial absence and dilation
Right ventricular angiography with thin-walled right ventricle
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominating
other: Histopathology confirming absence of right ventricular myocardium with preserved endocardium and epicardium

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
Right ventricular wall thinning but not complete absence
Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
Right atrial enlargement rather than right ventricular myocardial absence

redFlags: Severe right ventricular dilation with wall thinning
Signs of right heart failure in neonates or infants
references: James TN. Uhl's anomaly: congenital absence of the right ventricular myocardium. Circulation. 1972;45(3):589-95.
Basso C, et al. Uhl's anomaly: a rare cause of right ventricular failure and sudden death. Cardiovasc Pathol. 2004;13(3):153-7.
